To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) for binary-response experiments with random block effects, designs that are optimal for marginal modelling are typically also optimal for conditional modelling, but (2) for experiments with strong dependence between observations within blocks, designs that are asymptotically optimal for conditional modelling are typically more efficient than those for marginal modelling.

the asymptotic approximation to the information matrix is accurate for experiments in which there is strong dependence within blocks; that kriging interpolation is a useful alternative to Monte Carlo approximations of the information matrix; and that the use of marginal models to derive optimal designs for conditional modelling is generally suboptimal.

(i) for binary-response experiments exhibiting strong dependence between observations within a block, optimal designs for marginal models are typically inefficient for conditional modelling; (ii) for such experiments, pseudo-Bayesian optimal designs are more efficient for conditional modelling than optimal designs from closed forms of marginal models; and (iii) for experiments exhibiting weak dependence between observations within blocks, optimal designs from closed form approximations to marginal models are efficient for conditional modelling, and pseudo-Bayesian optimality is unnecessary.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the optimal design for estimating a conditional model can often be obtained by using a design that is optimal for a corresponding marginal model, provided that the marginal model is estimated using an appropriate correction for attenuation of the model parameters.

the use of marginal models to design experiments with random block effects can lead to highly inefficient designs, but that the problem can be avoided with the help of asymptotic information approximations and/or Monte Carlo kriging interpolations.
, for the design of experiments with binary responses, the use of marginal models for the design is not necessarily justified, and the design should be based on conditional models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of model for design purposes can have a significant impact on design efficiency.
the choice of design for a GLMM depends on the modelling framework, and should not be made without careful consideration.
